nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Closed-loop systems|Waste minimization strategies_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is industrial waste minimization considered a strategic target for companies according to the SCP model?
nodes.answer: Industrial waste minimization is considered a strategic target for companies according to the SCP model because it offers significant durable advantages, such as cost savings, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Closed-loop systems|Waste minimization strategies_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is hazardous waste minimization rarely seen as a strategic business goal by companies?
nodes.answer: Hazardous waste minimization is rarely seen as a strategic business goal by companies due to the lack of competences among managers to implement concrete actions of Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP) in operations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Closed-loop systems|Waste minimization strategies_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the goal of Life Cycle Management (LCM)?
nodes.answer: The goal of Life Cycle Management (LCM) is to minimize environmental and socio-economic burdens over the entire life cycle of a product or service.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Closed-loop systems|Waste minimization strategies_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the "Set in Order" principle, Seton, contribute to time savings in waste management?
nodes.answer: The "Set in Order" principle, Seton, contributes to time savings in waste management by organizing waste management tools and pathways efficiently, resulting in less time wasted in locating and using the necessary tools, ultimately improving overall efficiency.
